_comment: Encoding contract for apps/web/public/images, shared by scripts/reencode-catalogue-images.mjs and tests/scripts/test_image_encoding.py so the converter and the guard cannot drift apart. See #96. maxDimension 1024 is the originals' own size: the point of this conversion is the encoding, not the resolution, and downscaling below 1024 starves the product detail page on 2x screens, which ask for 1100 device pixels.
_fullBleed: Images exempt from the contract above -- not 'optimised some other way'. hero and contact-bg used to be here; #158 re-encoded them to WebP at q80 (814 KiB -> 78, 443 -> 214) and moved them into the contract. That gains the format and dimension checks. It gains little on weight: they are two files in a corpus whose mean _weights records, and only the per-file ceiling touches them individually, where hero has 8x of headroom and contact-bg 3x. It also binds them to maxDimension, which is shared with the catalogue and with the srcset ceiling derived from it in next.config.js -- so a sharper background needs those two separated first, not the number raised. about/mission.png stays exempt because it is a lossless source the optimiser re-encodes on every request, so converting it makes the delivered image a third generation; and because at 604 CSS px on a 2x screen it already wants more source than its 1024 provides. The field name is a leftover -- see #165. Note the two backgrounds are q80, not the q90 above: that field is the converter's default for catalogue photographs the optimiser re-encodes, and these are terminal and sit under a multiply blend and a 40% wash, where q80 measured invisible. Nothing records or checks an encoder setting after the fact, so this sentence is the only place that difference exists.
_weights: Two ceilings that catch different mistakes. This is the only place the measurements are written down; the guard points here rather than restating them. Shipped, the 854 average 184 KiB with the largest at 446 KiB. maxBytes (640 KiB) fails if any single image exceeds it, which is what a lossless re-encode does immediately -- measured on a 78-image sample, lossless averages 858 KiB and puts 68% of files over the ceiling. maxMeanBytes (256 KiB) exists for the mistake that stays under it everywhere: a quality bump. Same sample, mean by setting -- q90 187 KiB (shipped), q92 214, q93 232, q94 250, q95 270, q98 336, and none of those put a single file over 640 KiB. So the mean ceiling bites from about q95 upward, at roughly 39% headroom over what is shipped.
_notCaught: A bump to about q94 or below (mean 250 KiB) passes both, as does a partial regression affecting a minority of the catalogue -- see the docstring on test_catalogue_mean_weight_is_within_the_ceiling. These guards catch a conversion run at the wrong setting, not a hand-edited subset.
